answer:
Headline results of run /home/hyoklee/poro/agent/results/run_20261115T155359Z_s20 (stride 20), read read-only via `python3 ~/poro/agent/report.py <run>` (no PBS jobs submitted, hazard.py not run):

- Records analysed: 759 (2016-03-18T02:09:17Z to 2016-03-26T00:59:44Z, 3.314% of the time window)
- Anomalous records (|robust z| > 5): 57
- DAS detections: 62 in 53 records; relative b 0.9849 (34 above Mc)
- Context: pumping injected 4.654e+05 m3, extracted 5.059e+05 m3, net -4.048e+04 m3 over 15.96 days; catalogue (GDR 859, LBNL/NCEDC March 2016) lists 5 events, ML -0.48 to 0.07

CALIBRATED (catalogue-based, Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5; LBNL catalogue magnitudes) — seismogenic index Sigma and P(Mw>=5.5) per year per b scenario:
- b = 1.0:  Sigma = -5.449,  P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.0001198  (P over observed volume 5.236e-06; P(M>=3)/yr 0.03719)
- b = 0.73: Sigma = -5.319,  P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.004922   (P over observed volume 0.0002155; P(M>=3)/yr 0.2809)
- b = 0.65: Sigma = -5.281,  P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.01474    (P over observed volume 0.0006484; P(M>=3)/yr 0.4653)

UPPER BOUND (DAS-based, uncalibrated magnitudes; every detection counted as an event at or above the catalogue Mc, so it over-counts):
- b = 0.9849, Sigma = -2.698, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842

Which is which: the per-b table (b = 1.0 / 0.73 / 0.65) is the CALIBRATED probability from the LBNL/NCEDC catalogue (Shapiro et al. 2021 Eq. 5). The single DAS-based value (b 0.9849, P(M>=5.5)/yr = 0.07842) is the UPPER BOUND using uncalibrated DAS magnitudes and over-counts because all 62 detections are treated as events at or above Mc. Even at the most pessimistic calibrated b = 0.65, P(Mw>=5.5) is ~0.015/yr — far below the DAS upper bound — so a Pohang-like Mw>=5.5 event is unlikely on these catalogue-calibrated numbers.
